newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee cuts losses by the close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee cuts losses by the close.

text.p: Nearby LIFFE coffee futures trimmed some losses to end Monday near their highs after players absorbed the less friendly crop estimates from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).
Traders said overall, London held pretty well with roaster buying helping nearby contracts to stay well above their session's floor.
Funds were also seen rolling forward their July positions further out into September. Arbitrage buying and selling against New York was also noted in the afternoon.
By the close, September stood $7 down at $1,778 a tonne and well above the day's low at $1,720. Its intraday peak was $1,780.

The USDA said late on Friday that Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop could hit 28 million 60-kg bags, up from 27.5 million in 1996/97. It put world 1997/98 production at 103.7 million against 100.7 million in 1996/97.
Traders from Brazil to Indonesia have criticised the USDA estimates, which they said differed vastly from their own forecasts.
Volume reached 5,800 lots, inflated by July/Sept switches which changed hands at $27-$30.
U.S. Green Coffee Association is expected to release its May stock numbers after the close of the New York trading. Traders said the data were expected to show an increase of 200,000-300,000 bags.
Earlier on Monday, LIFFE's May certified stock data fell to 881 fiove-tonne lots from 4,858 lots in April.
But traders said data showed no real suprise in view of the new grading terms which come into effect with the July contract onwards.
Elsewhere, Brazil, confirming earlier trade expectation, has told the Association of Coffee Producing Countries that it was likely to exceed the 12 million bag export quota for the year to June 30.
